## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and catalog data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

The *Godhajātaka* (Ja 138) is a canonical birth-story preserved in the *Jātaka* collection of the Khuddaka Nikāya. Set in the Jetavana monastery, the frame story relates that the Buddha addressed a deceitful monk (*kuhaka*) and delivered a tale of the past to expose his hypocritical nature [Fausböll 1877]. In the past, during the reign of King Brahmadatta of Bārāṇasī, the Bodhisatta was reborn as a lizard (*godha*) living in an anthill near a forest hermitage [Fausböll 1877]. When an unscrupulous, deceitful ascetic (*kūṭatāpasa*) attempted to snare and kill the lizard to eat its meat, the Bodhisatta eluded him by taking refuge inside his mound and delivered the moralizing stanza opening with *Kiṁ te jaṭāhi dummedha* ("What is the use of your matted hair, you fool?") [Fausböll 1877]. Concluding the narrative (*samodhāna*), the Buddha identifies the false ascetic with the hypocritical monk, an earlier virtuous ascetic with Sāriputta, and the lizard with himself [Fausböll 1877].
